prerequisites: Units of measurement and dimensions of physical quantities (compulsory)
concepts of force, moment of a force, work and energy (compulsory)

learning_outcomes.text: The student will gain a basic understanding of the mechanical behaviour within the elastic range of plane structures subjected to point and distributed loads, and of the determination of stress and strain states in elastic solids, with the help of advanced textbooks.

The student will acquire knowledge and skills that will enable him/her to analyse the structural behaviour and the stress/strain state of plane structures in the linear elastic range, solving the proposed problems with a professional approach.

The student will gain the autonomous ability to identify and propose appropriate procedures for the calculation of stresses and strains in both statically determinate and statically indeterminate plane structures operating in the linear elastic range.

The student will gain the capability of describing to specialists and non-specialists the problems to tackle and the solutions to adopt concerning the stress-strain analysis of plane structures, making use of valid technical reasoning.

The student will gain the ability to deal with typical issues related to the study of plane structures operating in the elastic range, developing the necessary theoretical skills to undertake more advanced studies in the future.

syllabus_topics: Forces and moments, couples of forces, equivalent force systems
Constraints, external loads, structural elements, materials
Geometry of masses: static moments, centres of mass (or centroids), Varignon’s theorem, moments of inertia, Huygens’ theorem, principal moments and directions, Mohr’s representation

Kinematic analysis of beam systems: degrees of freedom and of constraints, internal and external constraints, statically under-constrained/determinate/indeterminate structures, theorems of kinematic chains
Static analysis of beam systems: equations of statics, support reactions
Statically determinate structures: determination of support reactions and internal actions

Mechanics of solids: analysis of deformation (small displacements kinematics, components of rigid motion and deformation, principal components and directions of deformation, compatibility conditions), analysis of stress (stress tensor, Cauchy’s theorem, principal components and directions of stress, invariants of the tensor, Mohr’s representations, plane stress states), equations of balance, boundary conditions
Basic laws of elasticity: elastic constitutive law, special case of isotropy, Hooke’s law, Lamé’s constants, engineering meaning of elastic constants
De Saint Venant’s problems: axial force, pure and bi-axial bending, coupled axial force and bending, shear, torsion
Principle of Virtual Work: determination of hyperstatic support reactions and displacements

assessment_methods.method: Written test: calculation of static moments, centroid’s position, moments of second order and principal axes of inertia of a plane figure
Written test: solution of a plane isostatic structure
Written test: solution of a plane hyperstatic structure
Oral test: determination of the stress state in a cross-section of a simple structure
Oral test: question concerning the theory developed during the frontal lectures

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and oral test. The maximum mark of the written test will be 30, and a minimum mark of 18/30 is required to be admitted to the oral test. To pass the exam with the minimum mark (18/30), the student must show basic knowledge of statics and elastic constitutive laws, calculate internal actions and draw diagrams, and determine the stress state in a prismatic beam. To achieve the maximum mark (30/30 e lode), excellent knowledge of all course topics is required.
